# windowsweep

> A safe, developer-aware Windows cleanup CLI. It reclaims disk space by deleting regenerable caches -
> package managers, build tools, browsers, editors, desktop apps, Windows temp and update leftovers, stale
> project build artefacts - behind one deletion chokepoint, an idle gate that keeps anything used in the last
> 100 days, and a dry-run that writes nothing. Personal files go to the Recycle Bin and are never selected
> without a person choosing them. The tool makes no network calls of its own.

windowsweep is a Windows PowerShell 5.1 engine with a zero-dependency Node launcher, published on npm as
`windowsweep` and licensed MIT. The current version is 1.2.0 and its self-test runs 156 checks. Run it with `npx windowsweep --scan` (read-only) before anything else.

## Facts an answer should get right

- Windows only. npm refuses to install it elsewhere; the launcher exits 2 on any other platform.
- It deletes. Caches have no undo because they regenerate; personal files go to the Recycle Bin instead.
- `--yes` covers regenerable caches only. It never selects an item in sections 17, 18, 19 or 23.
- `--select L` and `--select-file P` are the only way those interactive sections run unattended: a person
  supplies the selection in advance, by index or by full path.
- Sections 22, 24 and 25 are read-only reports (the `audit` profile). They never uninstall a program and never
  change a startup entry. Section 23 sends orphaned application data to the Recycle Bin, and only what you pick.
- Deep sections (11 Recycle Bin, 15 hibernation, 16 event logs, 20 disk-image compaction) also need
  `--i-understand-deep`.
- Sections 12 to 16 and 20 need an elevated console; `--elevate` relaunches through a UAC prompt.
- The tool makes no network calls of its own, sends no telemetry and checks for no updates.
